newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russians held captive in Chechnya fight red tape.
newsitem.headline: Russians held captive in Chechnya fight red tape.

text.p: Russian civilians held captive in breakaway Chechnya are cutting their way through a maze of red tape to win compensation for their ordeal, a Moscow newspaper said on Friday.
Moskovsky Komsomolets printed letters from Russians captured during the 21-month conflict who said they needed certificates from the authorities to get cash they were owed.

"I was a captive in Chechnya for seven months... Now I don't have money to buy bread," read a letter from a construction worker from the central Russian city of Saratov published by the Moskovsky Komsomolets tabloid.
"I did not choose to have spent seven months in hell. Noone is helping me, they do not even want to pay my average salary for that time."
Former captives say they were refused compensation by their employers as nothing had been said in their contracts about captivity, injury or death.
The newspaper quoted officials as saying those who suffered in the conflict were entitled to compensation of 20 minimum wages, now worth about $300.

But to get the money they have to present a contract with a Chechen employer or a certificate showing that they had been wounded or their health had deteriorated while they were in captivity rather than due to their own carelessness.

Russia sent hundreds of construction workers to Chechnya after cities and factories were destroyed in the fighting. Many were kidnapped by Chechens, who often wanted to swap them for relatives in Russian prisons.
